text: LMA is represented in CPCS as Body, Effort, Shape, and Space.
Effort factors are Weight, Time, Space, and Flow with bipolar qualities.
Signed-to-unit axis conversion is a CPCS normalization, not official LMA notation.
LMA expert labels show nonzero inter-rater disagreement and require reliability reporting.
Labanotation has been represented in XML and ontology forms.
Bartenieff Basic Six exercises differ from six connectivity patterns.
Cross-lateral organization is a useful prior for contralateral locomotion and rotational actions.
The exact seven-phase CPCS sequence is not a universal established standard.
Gesture stroke is the obligatory meaning-bearing phase in McNeill/Kendon-style analysis; other phases can be optional.
BML exposes synchronization points including start, ready, stroke and end-related points.
FACS codes visible facial action, not emotion or deception directly.
A flat count of 44 AUs depends on code grouping and implementation convention.
OpenFace reports presence and 0–5 intensity for a subset of AUs.
PSPI uses AU4 + max(AU6,AU7) + max(AU9,AU10) + AU43.
Micro-expression duration thresholds vary across datasets and are not a universal deception rule.
Kinematics describes motion; force estimation requires dynamics assumptions or measurements.
OpenCap estimates movement dynamics from smartphone video with a musculoskeletal pipeline.
Pose2Sim supports multiview markerless kinematics and inverse-kinematics workflows.
Published punch velocities/forces are protocol- and population-specific, not universal limits.
Intent-to-motion mappings are probabilistic and culture/context conditioned.
BEAT is a large multimodal conversational gesture dataset with emotion and multiple languages.
EMOTE parameterizes expressive motion with Effort and Shape.
There is no validated universal visible-motion signature for deception.
HICO-DET supplies a broad human-object interaction verb/object vocabulary.
Inter-X focuses on versatile two-person interaction data.
Generated interaction can remain visually plausible while violating contact physics.
LMA Weight is not equal to force in newtons.
Kinetic-chain sequencing can be represented as temporal segment transfer but is task specific.
Apparent motion depends on relative camera/subject motion, projection and depth.
180-degree, 30-degree and match-on-action are continuity conventions, not physical laws.
Editing rhythm includes timing, pacing, trajectory phrasing, tension and release.
AIST++ supports music/dance alignment research.
VAD represents affect along valence, arousal and dominance dimensions.
The NRC VAD lexicon should be referenced under its terms, not redistributed in this package.
Lexical VAD ratings do not directly equal embodied performance measurements.
Motion style can be transferred with learned models, including body-part-local approaches.
Content/style disentanglement does not guarantee preservation of action or contact.
No broadly validated full-BESS real-time OpenFace-equivalent detector was identified.
BoME contains 1,600 clips with expert labels for 11 selected LMA motor elements.
Weight and Flow are harder to infer visually than geometric Space/Time features.
LabanWRML and ChoosenMove were not verified as established detector systems under those names.
scope: search gap; absence cannot be certain

text: Veo 3.1 documentation exposes structured duration, aspect, resolution, seed and reference/image controls with variant-specific constraints.
Kling VIDEO 3.0 documents 3–15 second multi-shot generation and references/audio on current surfaces.
Runway Gen-4.5 documents 2–10 second generation and 24/25 fps on its current guide.
Runway Act-Two uses a driving performance and character input, with different behavior for image versus video character modes.
Ray 3.2 Modify exposes Motion/Structure controls and Poses/Blocking behavior.
Adobe Firefly documents a camera-motion reference workflow with input constraints and control incompatibilities.
OpenAI ended Sora web/app on 2026-04-26 and schedules Sora API end for 2026-09-24.
UI and API surfaces must be versioned separately.
Unsupported canonical fields must remain visible in a loss report.
